chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of God and their derivation — from what is 'Allah' derived?

He said: So he said to me: 'O Hisham! Allah is derived from ilah (deity), and ilah requires a worshipper (ma'luh). And the name is other than the named. So whoever worships the name without the meaning (reality) has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything; and whoever worships the name and the meaning has disbelieved and worshipped two; and whoever worships the meaning without the name — that is tawhid. Do you understand, O Hisham?'

He said: So I said, 'Give me more.' He said: 'Indeed, God has ninety-nine names. If the name were the named, then every one of them would be a deity. But God is a meaning (reality) toward which these names point, and all of them are other than Him. O Hisham! Bread is a name for food, water is a name for the drink, cloth is a name for what is worn, fire is a name for what burns. Do you understand, O Hisham, an understanding with which you can repel and fight our enemies and those who take others alongside God — Majestic and Mighty?' I said: 'Yes.'
He said: So he said: 'May God benefit you with it and affirm you, O Hisham.' Hisham said: By God, no one overcame me regarding tawhid until I reached my present station.

key_terms.إله: Ilah — deity, that which is worshipped; the root from which Allah is derived
key_terms.الاسم: The name — a linguistic designation, a pointer
key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — divine unity; worshipping the Reality alone
key_terms.المسمى: The named — the actual reality being designated
key_terms.المعنى: The meaning/reality — the actual Divine Being being pointed to
key_terms.مأكولاً: Worshipper, one who worships (the ilah requires a ma'luh)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Name of God and God Himself according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a celebrated theological exchange between Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) concerning the ontological distinction between God's Names and God's essential reality. The Imam articulates a precise philosophical point: the word 'Allah' is linguistically derived from 'ilah' (deity/worshipped one), and a deity by definition requires a worshipper. However, the name itself — as a linguistic label — is not identical to the Divine Reality it designates. Worshipping only the label without understanding the transcendent reality is kufr (disbelief); equally, treating the name as a second entity alongside the reality is polytheism (worshipping two). True tawhid consists in directing worship exclusively to the Divine Reality, using names merely as pointers. This teaching was conveyed to Hisham ibn al-Hakam, the foremost Imami theologian of his era, who used this insight as the cornerstone of his argumentation against opponents of Imami theology in the disputatious intellectual environment of early Abbasid Baghdad.
